{{nihongo|'''Sugawara Tenmangū'''|菅原天満宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

[[File:Sugahara-jinja (Nara), entrance.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]'''Sugawara Tenmangu'' (Sugawara Tenmangu) is located in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Nara (city)|Q169134|qid=Q169134}} Sugawara Higashi 1-chome.{{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}}. In {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. Also known as ``Sugawara Shrine''. It is known as a shrine related to the ancient clans {{ill|Haji clan|Q10927758|qid=Q10927758}} and {{ill|Sugawara clan|Q1771125|qid=Q1771125}}.

=== Enshrined God ===
The following three deities are enshrined. </ref>.
* {{ill|Ame no Hohi|Q10940685|qid=Q10940685|lt=Amenohohi no Mikoto}} (Amenohohi no Mikoto)
* {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|Q965742|qid=Q965742|lt=Nominosukune no Mikoto}} (Nominosukune no Mikoto)
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} (SugaharaMichizaneko)

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, the enshrined deity is listed as 1 {{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1982}}. According to the shrine's legend, there was originally one enshrined deity, Tenho Nichimiko, but later Nomi no Sukune and Sugawara Michizane were enshrined, making the number three.

=== About the enshrined deity ===The main enshrined deity, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|Q10940685|qid=Q10940685|lt=Amenohohi}}, is described in ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'' as ``Kore Izumo. As you can see, he became the ancestor god of the ancient clan '''{{ill|Haji clan|Q10927758|qid=Q10927758}}'' (Hajiuji, Hajiren and later Haji Sukune). The Haji clan is the {{ill|Tomonomiyatsuko|Q11381545|qid=Q11381545}} clan of Hajibu, which is responsible for the production of {{ill|Haniwa|ar|هانيوا|ca|Haniwa|cs|Haniwa|de|Haniwa|eo|Haniva|es|Haniwa|fi|Haniwa|fr|Haniwa|hu|Haniva|id|Haniwa|it|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|mk|Ханива|nl|Haniwa|pl|Haniwa|pt|Haniwa|ru|Ханива|sr|Ханива|sv|Haniwa|th|ฮานิวะ|tr|Haniwa|uk|Ханіва|zh|埴轮|qid=Q849376}}, {{ill|Earthenware|Q1377111|qid=Q1377111}}, funerals, and {{ill|mausoleum|Q65292090|qid=Q65292090}} {{Sfn| The Haji clan (ancient clan) |2010}}, the distant ancestor of the Haji clan, {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|Q965742|qid=Q965742}}, is also the person whose Haniwa tradition is recorded in the Nihon Shoki. This Haji clan has four limbs, which appear as "four bells," in an article dated December 30, 9th year of {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} ({{ill|790|Q31147|qid=Q31147}}) of "{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}". These are {{ill|Izumi Province|ca|Província d'Izumi|ckb|پارێزگای ئیزومی|cs|Provincie Izumi|de|Provinz Izumi|es|Provincia de Izumi|fa|ولایت ایزومی|fr|Province d'Izumi|gl|Provincia de Izumi|hak|Izumi-koet|id|Provinsi Izumi|it|Izumi (provincia)|ja|和泉国|ko|이즈미국|lt|Idzumio žemė|nl|Izumi (provincie)|pt|Província de Izumi|ru|Идзуми (провинция)|simple|Izumi Province|sk|Izumi (provincia)|sr|Провинција Изуми|tr|Izumi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ідзумі|zh|和泉國|zh_min_nan|Izumi-kok|zh_yue|和泉國|qid=Q1047117}} Mozu, {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} Sugawara, Yamato Province Akishino, {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}{{ jalink|Shiki District|Q11491125}}, {{ill|Tajihinokōri district|Q11368538|qid=Q11368538}} are huge tumulus groups ({{ill|Mozu Tombs|Q4250584|qid=Q4250584}}, {{jalink|Saki Dunretsu Kofun {{Sfn|Hashi clan (ancient clan)|2010}}{{Sfn|Hashi (ancient clan encyclopedia)|2015}}, which corresponds to the site of the burial mound group|Q11383489|Saki kofun group}}/{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Q4250076|qid=Q4250076}}). Of the four tribes, the Mozu, Sugawara, and Akishino tribes were formed around the end of {{ill|8th century|Q8086|qid=Q8086}}, respectively by the Oeda clan (later {{ill|Ōe clan|Q11436863|qid=Q11436863}}) and {{ill|Ōe clan|Q11436863|qid=Q11436863}}. |Sugawara clan|Q1771125}} and {{ill|Akishino clan|Q65277285|qid=Q65277285}}.The place name ``Sugawara'' means the grassland and natural habitat of {{ill|Carex|Q158501|qid=Q158501|lt=Sedge}} (sedge), and the name originally referred to the vast hilly area west of {{ill|Heijō Palace|Q211585|qid=Q211585}} {{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Shinai Shrine)|1982}}. Regarding the Haji clan branch clan in the Sugawara area, the ``Suga family biographies'' also states that the Haji clan resides as ``Since then, the Dobe clan has lived in Sugawara Fushimi Village'' {{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. In fact, the existence of the Haniwa kiln ruins of the late Sugawara Higashi Ruins (designated historical site by Nara City) from the late {{ill|Kofun period|af|Kofun-tydperk|ar|فترة كوفون|az|Kofun dövrü|be|Кафун|bg|Кофун|bn|কোফুন যুগ|ca|Període Kofun|cs|Období Kofun|de|Kofun-Zeit|eo|Kofun-epoko|es|Período Kofun|eu|Kofun aroa|fa|دوره کوفون|fi|Kofun-kausi|fr|Période Kofun|he|תקופת קופון|hr|Razdoblje Kofun|hu|Kofun-kor|id|Zaman Kofun|it|Periodo Kofun|ja|古墳時代|ko|고훈 시대|lt|Kofun laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Kofun|nl|Kofunperiode|pl|Kofun (okres)|pt|Período Kofun|ro|Perioada Kofun|ru|Период Кофун|sh|Kofunski period|simple|Kofun period|sk|Obdobie Kofun|sl|Obdobje Kofun|sr|Кофун период|sv|Kofunperioden|th|ยุคโคฟุง|tl|Panahong Kofun|tr|Kofun Dönemi|uk|Період Кофун|vi|Thời kỳ Kofun|wuu|古坟时代|zh|古坟时代|zh_min_nan|Kohun sî-tāi|zh_yue|古墳時代|qid=Q459939}} area is known to support the existence of the Haji clan. Sugawara Higashi Ruins Haniwa Kiln Ruins] (Nara City homepage). </ref>It is also noteworthy that the area of ​​worship of Sugawara Shrine almost coincides with the distribution range of the Haji clan. In addition to Sugawara Shrine, history books also include {{ill|Hōraiyama Kofun|Q11452574|qid=Q11452574|lt=Sugawara Fushimi Toryo}} ({{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}} tomb) and Sugawara Fushimi West Mausoleum ({{ill|Emperor Ankō|Q361010|qid=Q361010}} tomb).・It is known that the name of Sugawara-dera Temple (currently {{ill|Kikō-ji|Q11419051|qid=Q11419051}}) is derived from the place name of this area, and the name of the Sugawara clan is also said to be derived from the name of this area {{Sfn|Sugawara clan (ancient clan)|2010}}. The rituals at Sugawara Shrine are thought to have originated when the Haji clan of Sugawara (later known as the Sugawara clan) worshiped their ancestral deity, but in later generations it became the birthplace of Michizane Sugawara. Some theories arose, and it is currently worshiped as a shrine of {{ill|Tenjin faith|Q66890725|qid=Q66890725}} {{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1982}}.

=== History ===
Founding date is unknown. As mentioned above, it is presumed that the Haji clan (later {{ill|Sugawara clan|Q1771125|qid=Q1771125}}), whose home base was {{ill|Korean clans|Q846706|qid=Q846706}}, worshiped their ancestral deity. Later, when Sugawara-dera Temple ({{ill|Kikō-ji|Q11419051|qid=Q11419051}}) was built in the southwest, it became its guardian shrine, and it came to be called both Sugawara Shrine and Kikoji Tenmangu Shrine.

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=In the Shinmeicho}}, ``Sugawara Shrine'' is listed in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}{{ill|Soejimo district|Q11560415|qid=Q11560415}}, and it is listed as a Shikinai Shrine {{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1982}}.According to the shrine's biography, the shrine was destroyed by military fire during the {{ill|Bunki|Q1324885|qid=Q1324885}} years ({{ill|1501|Q6131|qid=Q6131}} - {{ill|1504|Q6148|qid=Q6148}}), and also during the {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} years ({{ill|1688|Q7671|qid=Q7671}} - There was also a fire in {{ill|1704|Q6824|qid=Q6824}}). {{ill|Kanpō|Q1145798|qid=Q1145798}} years ({{ill|1741|Q7573|qid=Q7573}} - {{ill|1744|Q7583|qid=Q7583}}) in {{ill|Kōfuku-ji|Q1070863|qid=Q1070863}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ichijoin}}It is said that it was rebuilt by order of the Imperial Prince Miya Makoto.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, it became independent from Kikoji Temple due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}. In {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was listed as ``Sugawara Shrine'' in {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1982}}. In {{ill|2002|Q1987|qid=Q1987}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}14), it was renamed to "Sugawara Tenmangu Shrine."

=== Festival ===
The festivals held annually at Sugawara Tenmangu Shrine are as follows.
* Monthly festival (25th of every month)
* Onda Festival (February 25th)
* Nara Fude Festival (March equinox)
* Birthday Festival, Shinto Ritual (June 25th)
* Regular festival (the day before Sports Day in October)
* Niinamesai (November 25th)
